name: Pangolin Addon (CLI)
description: Installs the official Pangolin CLI on the Proxmox host or into an existing LXC and enables Site mode (`pangolin up site` — the Newt replacement), Machine Client mode (`pangolin up client` — VPN), or both. One binary, two components. The CLI download is sha256-verified, services run through the upstream CLI, and existing addon or standalone Newt installs are migrated in place.

notes.text: Components: Site tunnel (expose private resources to Pangolin, userspace WireGuard, no TUN) and/or Machine client (join the host/LXC into the Pangolin network as a device, needs /dev/net/tun). The CLI binary installs once and both components can run side by side as separate services (`pangolin-site` and `pangolin-client`).
Targets: the Proxmox host or an existing LXC running Debian 12+, Ubuntu 22.04+, or Alpine 3.20+. Debian and Ubuntu use systemd; Alpine uses OpenRC with `supervise-daemon`.
Run on the Proxmox host (not inside a container). Choose Proxmox host or an existing LXC, then select which components and enter credentials.
Host install: the host is directly connected to Pangolin (site can expose everything the host can reach; client joins the whole host to the VPN). Prefer an existing LXC for isolation.

Site mode: use the Site ID + secret from the Pangolin dashboard (works on every Pangolin edition), or a site provisioning key (tier3/enterprise only; dashboard Settings → Provisioning → Keys). With "approve new sites" disabled, the site stays pending until an operator approves it. A provisioning key also takes an optional site name (default: the target hostname).

Reconfiguring an existing site with a provisioning key creates a second server-side site; delete the old site in the dashboard. Set `var_reconfigure=1` to replace an existing local site configuration; without it a verified site is reused.

Client mode: create a machine client in the Pangolin dashboard first, then copy the client ID, secret, and endpoint. On an LXC the addon adds /dev/net/tun passthrough and restarts the CT gracefully only when the config changes; on the host it loads the tun module and fails early when /dev/net/tun is unavailable.

The CLI is installed at /usr/local/bin/pangolin only from the official fosrl/cli release, after its sha256 digest and reported version are verified. The accepted artifact is recorded in /var/lib/pangolin/cli.json. Minimum CLI version 0.21.0. Pin `var_pangolin_cli_version` and supply `var_pangolin_cli_sha256` when pinning a version other than the latest.

Configuration: /etc/pangolin/site.json (mode 0600) and /etc/pangolin/pangolin-client.env (mode 0600, contains the client secret). Both components use /etc/pangolin. The CLI installs the systemd units; on Alpine the addon writes OpenRC units that run the CLI.

Inspect or remove the services with the upstream CLI: `pangolin service status site|client`, `pangolin service logs site|client`, `pangolin service uninstall site|client`. From the host for an LXC, prefix the command with `pct exec <CTID> --`.

Update by re-running the addon; the latest CLI is downloaded and verified again, and an already verified version is reused. The old `update-pangolin-site` / `update-pangolin-cli` wrappers are deprecated and are not installed by new installs; they bypass the sha256 check, so do not rely on them.

Existing addon installs and standalone Newt installs (with /etc/newt/newt.env) are detected and migrated in place, reusing the existing credentials. Replaced files are backed up under /var/lib/pangolin/backup, and legacy cleanup runs only after the replacement component verifies.

Unattended (site, host, provisioning key): `var_mode=site var_target=host var_pangolin_endpoint=https://pangolin.example.com var_site_provisioning_key=spk-... var_site_name=NAME bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraad/proxmox-scripts/main/tools/addon/add-pangolin.sh)"`

Unattended (site, host, site ID + secret): `var_mode=site var_target=host var_pangolin_endpoint=https://pangolin.example.com var_site_id=ID var_site_secret=SECRET bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraad/proxmox-scripts/main/tools/addon/add-pangolin.sh)"`

Unattended (client, LXC): `var_mode=client var_target=101 var_pangolin_endpoint=https://pangolin.example.com var_client_id=ID var_client_secret=SECRET bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraad/proxmox-scripts/main/tools/addon/add-pangolin.sh)"`
Unattended (both, LXC): use `var_mode=both` and supply `var_site_id`/`var_site_secret` (or `var_site_provisioning_key`) plus `var_client_id`/`var_client_secret`.

Other variables: `var_reconfigure=1` replaces an existing verified site configuration, `var_pangolin_cli_version` and `var_pangolin_cli_sha256` pin the binary, and `PANGOLIN_DRY_RUN=1` validates the inputs and prints the plan without changing the host.

Legacy aliases `var_newt_id` / `var_newt_secret` map to the site credentials. The deprecated wrapper URLs `tools/addon/add-pangolin-site.sh` (site), `tools/addon/add-pangolin-cli.sh` (client), and `tools/addon/add-newt.sh` (site alias) still work and call the unified addon.
